api/Koffing.Blocks.Block.html.summary: Class Block Namespace Koffing.Blocks Assembly Koffing.dll Abstract class representing a grouping of Tiles. public abstract class Block : IEnumerable<Tile>, IEnumerable, IBlock, IComparable<Block>, IEquatable<Block> Inheritance object Block Implements IEnumerable<Tile> IEnumerable IBlock IComparable<Block> IEquatable<Block> Derived Meld Wait Inherited Members object.Equals(object, object) object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) Extension Methods Extensions.NotationFromTiles(IEnumerable<Tile>) Remarks A block is a very generic grouping of Tiles. This should be the root class for all derived blocks as it provides some basic implementations of the major interfaces of IEnumerable<T>, IBlock, IComparable<T>, and IEquatable<T>. Constructors Block(IEnumerable<Tile>) Constructor. Optionally takes in an IEnumerable<T> of Tiles. public Block(IEnumerable<Tile> tiles = null) Parameters tiles IEnumerable<Tile> The Tiles that make up the block. Remarks In general, this (and the other constructors for derived classes) should not be used in favor of using IBlock static functions such as GetPossible(IEnumerable<Tile>) or the GetPossibleBlockSets(IEnumerable<Tile>) static helper function. Those methods will ensure that Blocks created correctly match their intended semantic meaning, such as Pungs having all the same tile or Chows having a sequence of tiles in the same suit. Fields _tiles The tiles that make up the block. protected readonly List<Tile> _tiles Field Value List<Tile> Properties this[int] Indexer. public Tile this[int index] { get; } Parameters index int Property Value Tile The Tile at index index in the Block. Methods CompareTo(Block) Compares the current instance with another object of the same type and returns an integer that indicates whether the current instance precedes, follows, or occurs in the same position in the sort order as the other object. public int CompareTo(Block that) Parameters that Block Returns int A value that indicates the relative order of the objects being compared. The return value has these meanings: Value Meaning Less than zero This instance precedes other in the sort order. Zero This instance occurs in the same position in the sort order as other. Greater than zero This instance follows other in the sort order. Remarks Comparison is done by comparing: if that is null (always 1) type (using GetHashCodeBasis()) the number of tiles in the block the actual tiles in the block (after sorting) using CompareTo(Tile). Equals(Block) Indicates whether the current object is equal to another object of the same type. public virtual bool Equals(Block thatBlock) Parameters thatBlock Block Returns bool true if the current object is equal to the other parameter; otherwise, false. Remarks Equality is determined by checking: if that is null (always false) type the number of tiles in the block the actual tiles in the block (after sorting) Equals(object) Determines whether the specified object is equal to the current object. public override bool Equals(object that) Parameters that object Returns bool true if the specified object is equal to the current object; otherwise, false. Remarks Equality is determined by checking: if that is null (always false) type then deferring to Equals(Block) GetEnumerator() Returns an enumerator that iterates through the collection. public IEnumerator<Tile> GetEnumerator() Returns IEnumerator<Tile> An enumerator that can be used to iterate through the collection. GetHashCode() Serves as the default hash function. public override int GetHashCode() Returns int A hash code for the current object. Remarks Calculates hash value using the value returned from GetHashCodeBasis() as a basis which is then exponentiated using an exponent created using that same basis and the hash codes for the tiles of the block. GetHashCodeBasis() Get the hash code basis representing this block type, which will be exponentiated as a part of calculating GetHashCode(). public static int GetHashCodeBasis() Returns int The basis to use when calculating hash codes for this block type. Returns IEnumerable<BlockSet> An IEnumerable<T> of BlockSets that can be created from tiles. Remarks As this is an abstract class not meant for concrete use, the implementation of this always throws NotImplementedException to encourage overriding. Exceptions NotImplementedException Thrown to encourage overriding. GetPossibleHelper(IEnumerable<Tile>, Type) Protected static helper function that can be used to simplify overrides of GetPossible(IEnumerable<Tile>). protected static IEnumerable<MadeBlockContext> GetPossibleHelper(IEnumerable<Tile> tiles, Type blockType) Parameters tiles IEnumerable<Tile> The Tiles to use to create MadeBlockContexts. blockType Type The Type of block to return Returns IEnumerable<MadeBlockContext> An IEnumerable<T> of MadeBlockContexts of type blockType. Examples As an example of such an override taken from GetPossible(IEnumerable<Tile>): public static new IEnumerable<MadeBlockContext> GetPossible(IEnumerable<Tile> tiles) { return GetPossibleHelper(tiles, typeof(Chow)).Distinct(); } Note that the call to Distinct<TSource>(IEnumerable<TSource>) is necessary, as this function does not do it itself. Remarks Most derived blocks have their logic for the GetPossible(IEnumerable<Tile>) function implemented as an override of GetPossibleForTile(Tile, IEnumerable<Tile>), as it is often easier to write logic around a single given tile. Rather than duplicating the logic to go through all distinct tiles and calling GetPossibleForTile(Tile, IEnumerable<Tile>) for each one, this function can be used instead. ToString() Returns a string that represents the current object. public override string ToString() Returns string A string that represents the current object. Remarks Prints the type (through ToString()) followed by ": " and then the MPSZ notation of the tiles as generated by NotationFromTiles(IEnumerable<Tile>).

It is only called if processing is enabled for this Node, which is done automatically if this method is overridden, and can be toggled with SetProcess(bool). Processing happens in order of Godot.Node.ProcessPriority, lower priority values are called first. Nodes with the same priority are processed in tree order, or top to bottom as seen in the editor (also known as pre-order traversal). Corresponds to the Godot.Node.NotificationProcess notification in _Notification(int). Note: This method is only called if the node is present in the scene tree (i.e. if it's not an orphan). Note: When the engine is struggling and the frame rate is lowered, delta will increase. When delta is increased, it's capped at a maximum of Godot.Engine.TimeScale * Godot.Engine.MaxPhysicsStepsPerFrame / Godot.Engine.PhysicsTicksPerSecond. As a result, accumulated delta may not represent real world time. Note: When --fixed-fps is enabled or the engine is running in Movie Maker mode (see Godot.MovieWriter), process delta will always be the same for every frame, regardless of how much time the frame took to render.
